stemMarkdown: A tank can be filled by pipe A in 10 hours and by pipe B in 15 hours. Pipe C, which empties the tank, can do so in 30 hours. If all three pipes are opened at once, how many hours will it take to fill the tank?
solutionMarkdown:
The rate of filling for pipe A is $\frac{1}{10}$ per hour and for pipe B, it is $\frac{1}{15}$. The rate at which pipe C empties the tank is $-\frac{1}{30}$. When all three are opened, their combined rate of filling the tank is:\
$$ \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{15} - \frac{1}{30} = \frac{3+2-1}{30} = \frac{4}{30} = \frac{2}{15} $$\
The combined rate means the tank will be filled in $\frac{15}{2}$ hours, or 7.5 hours.
altSolutionMarkdown:
An alternative approach: The LCM of 10, 15 and 30 is 30. If we consider this as the capacity (in units) for convenience:\
Pipe A fills 3 units/hour, Pipe B fills 2 units/hour, and Pipe C empties 1 unit/hour. Combined they fill:\
$$ 3 + 2 - 1 = 4 \text{ units/hour} $$\
The tank capacity is 30 units so it will take \\(\frac{30}{4} = 7.5 \\) hours.
